display.purpose: Page and section headings at 28px, weight 600, tracking 0.05em, line-height 1.1. Uppercase with balanced wrapping — the engraved editorial voice.

title.purpose: Card, Dialog and header titles at 20px, weight 600, tracking 0.05em, line-height 1.15. Uppercase with balanced wrapping — the workhorse structural voice.

label.purpose: Buttons, field labels, nav links, command headings and shortcuts. Uppercase 12px caps at weight 600, tracking 0.08em (0.96px), line-height 1.

body.purpose: Default copy and card content at 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.5 with text-wrap: pretty. Weight 500 is the light-on-dark compensation on the forest canvas and raised forest cards, one whole step above caption.

caption.purpose: Descriptions and hints at 14px, weight 400, line-height 1.5 with text-wrap: pretty — copy, never a caps label.

data.purpose: Quantities, counts and prices at 16px, weight 400, line-height 1.3. Tabular figures so columns of digits align; no Penpot equivalent for the numeric variant.

input.purpose: Form controls only, owned by Input and Textarea. 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.5 — one size at every breakpoint; the old md:0.875rem step is gone.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default for color, background and border transitions on controls (Tailwind transition-all / transition-colors).

motion.name: layer-transition
motion.purpose: Dialog and popover open/close: fade plus a 95% zoom-in, on animate-in / animate-out.

motion.name: press-nudge
motion.purpose: Button active state. The only physical movement in the system.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one brass CTA on a view. Forest 950 text on Brass 500, cut square, caps label. Hover steps to Brass 400; press nudges 1px down.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: Tier-3 floating layer on the Forest 800 popover surface, held by its tone step, with no ring and no shadow. Opens at 100ms with a fade and 95% zoom; descriptions cap at the 65ch prose measure. Its dismissal is the footer’s ghost Закрыть — DialogFooter renders it for every dialog, ahead of the actions, and no dialog carries a corner ✕ (upstream shadcn’s default, removed on purpose); Escape and an outside press are bonus paths. The destructive action is Ember, per the destructive rule.

narrative.overview: Sklad is the working tool of a small atelier that builds physical goods by hand and runs the whole business itself. The world answers to that room: a single forest green, stepped from a near-black floor to a pale sage ink, holds every surface, every line and every word. Brass is the only thing that shines. The system is quiet by construction. Because recording a material receipt or a batch is a break in the work rather than a sitting-down task, the UI recedes: one content column, no ornament, no colour competing with the data. Identity is carried by geometry and material — one sans face in uppercase editorial caps, sharp unrounded corners, and depth built from tonal steps rather than floating cards. Hierarchy comes from type weight and from how light a surface is, not from borders drawn in a second colour. Reliability here is visual: numbers, counts and costs must be readable at a glance on a phone at the bench, and a destructive action must never be mistaken for an ordinary one. Every rule below exists to keep that reading honest.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only presentation; the light block in `tailwind.css` is documentation, not a shipped mode.
One hue for the whole world: forest (H≈131), stepped into nine tones that carry floor, surfaces, linework and text.
Surfaces are tone steps, never a second hue: floor `forest.950` → card `forest.850` → popover `forest.800`.
Brass has two jobs: hardware at `brass.500` (the CTA), highlight at `brass.300` (accent and focus ring).
Borders are decoration (1.40–1.67:1); every control edge owns `--control-border` and clears 3:1.
`rounded-none` on every shipped component — sharp sera geometry.
Depth by tonal layering only, never a shadow; surfaces carry no ring and no shadow.
Single-column `max-w-4xl` shell with a 4px spacing rhythm.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Brass is spent on at most one important thing per view. `brass.500` always carries `forest.950` text; `forest.100` on `brass.500` is 1.62:1 (1.11:1 on the highlight) and must never be used.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: The world is a single hue (H≈131). Surfaces, linework, text and charts all step through it; a second hue in a structural role is a bug, not a flavour. Ember is a signal, never a surface.

rules.name: The Border Is Decoration Rule
rules.body: `--border` is allowed to whisper (1.40–1.67:1). Anything a user is expected to see as a boundary — a control edge, an underline, a focus edge — uses `--control-border`, `--ring` or `--invalid`, all of which clear 3:1 against the surface they sit on.

rules.name: The No Raw Palette Rule
rules.body: Components reach for semantic tokens. Raw Tailwind palette colours (`text-green-600`, `bg-amber-500`) are off-system, in components and in Penpot alike.

rules.name: The Error Is Ember Rule
rules.body: Destruction and error are Ember: `--invalid` for the underline, `--destructive` (Ember fill, `forest.950` label) for the button or capsule that acts. Never `forest.100` on Ember (2.38:1); never Ember as a surface.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: `--muted-foreground` on any forest surface stays ≥ 4.5:1 (8.11 floor / 6.80 card). A control boundary clears 3:1 against the surface it actually sits on (`--control-border`: 3.02–3.96). Error and destructive clear 4.5:1 (5.21–6.21). Never communicate status by colour alone.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Manrope everywhere — copy, controls, headings and labels (`--font-heading` aliases `--font-sans`). No serif, no second display face, no designed mono. Geometry is expressed through caps headings and editorial spacing.

rules.name: The Body Floor Rule
rules.body: Unstyled text never lands on preflight defaults: the base `body` rule carries `type-body`, so raw `p`, `span`, `div` and reset headings inherit the body role (1rem / 500 / 1.5 / `pretty`) instead of 400-weight browser text. Roles still come from `Typography` or the matching `type-*` utility, which win the cascade.

rules.name: The Token-Or-Nothing Rule
rules.body: Never set type with raw utilities (`text-xs`, `text-sm`, `font-*`, `leading-*`, `tracking-*`) in project components. Go through `Typography`. Replace, don't layer: Tailwind emits raw size utilities _after_ the `type-*` utilities, so a leftover `text-sm` wins the cascade — and `cn()` will not resolve the collision. The scale is exposed as `@utility type-*`, not as `--text-*` theme keys, because `cn()` classifies unknown `text-*` strings as colors.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose never spans the shell. Copy caps at `--measure-prose` (65ch) and is applied in the prose slots — `CardDescription`, `DialogDescription`, `FieldDescription`, `CommandEmpty` — never on `type-body` itself: the role also covers full-width controls (`InputGroupText`, the command search field), which must keep their box. At the 1rem floor the `max-w-4xl` shell would otherwise run copy to ~109 characters per line; 65ch resolves to ~650px (Manrope's zero advance at 16px is 10px), which lands Cyrillic copy at ~75–79 characters per line.

rules.name: The Wrapping Rule
rules.body: Caps headings (`type-display`, `type-title`) carry `text-wrap: balance` so a two- or three-line title breaks evenly instead of orphaning a word; reading copy (`type-body`, `type-caption`) carries `text-wrap: pretty`, which stops Russian's short prepositions and conjunctions from stranding at a line end. Where the property is unsupported the declaration is simply dropped — no fallback is needed.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Content lives in one `max-w-4xl` column. New surfaces inherit the shell instead of introducing a second grid.

rules.name: The Tone-Only Rule
rules.body: To lift content, move one step up the ladder (950 → 850 → 800). Never add a shadow, and never a ring, to prove the lift — if a surface does not read as raised, its tone step is wrong.

rules.name: The Sharp Sera Rule
rules.body: `rounded-none` is the default and the shipped answer. If a component wants a radius, that is a system-level decision recorded here first — not a local `rounded-lg`.

dos: **Do** reach for `Button variant="outline"` for the app's default secondary action, and `variant="default"` (brass) for the one primary CTA on a view.
**Do** keep destructive/confirm actions visually distinct with `variant="destructive"` (Ember fill, `forest.950` label), and pair destructive intent with a Dialog confirmation.
**Do** put `forest.950` text on brass — `--primary-foreground` every time.
**Do** put every boundary that must be seen — control edges, underlines, focus edges — on `--control-border`, `--ring` or `--invalid`.
**Do** step surfaces up the forest ladder (950 → 850 → 800); that step is the only lift.
**Do** use `gap-*` stacks and the `max-w-4xl` shell for new surfaces.
**Do** keep `--muted-foreground` for secondary text and `--foreground` for body.
**Do** set all type through `Typography` / the `type-*` tokens.
**Do** use tabular figures (`type-data`) for any column of numbers.
**Do** chart with the main color palette: `--chart-1` for a single series, deeper steps in order for up to three, and direct labels past that.
**Do** re-run the rebind pass (`literal → apply token`) after editing a token value, in Penpot and in CSS.
**Do** verify the `--muted-foreground` pairing stays ≥ 4.5:1 when the forest ladder changes.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second hue into surfaces, linework or text — Ember is a signal, not a surface, and there is no second material family.
**Don't** ring or shadow a surface (card, dialog, command list) — they separate by tone alone; a border or shadow there is maintenance that reads as almost nothing.
**Don't** draw a control edge with `--border`; 1.40–1.67:1 is a whisper, not a boundary.
**Don't** render error as a coloured ink — the Ember capsule plus `--invalid` underline is the only recipe.
**Don't** put a corner ✕ on a dialog — dismissal is the footer's ghost `Закрыть`, which `DialogFooter` renders for every dialog (upstream shadcn's ✕ is removed on purpose).
**Don't** add radius, colors, fonts or shadows outside the token set above.
**Don't** introduce serif, mono or additional display faces, and don't use `font-mono` in project components.
**Don't** bypass semantic tokens with raw palette colors (`text-green-600` etc.).
**Don't** separate chart series with a second hue or with Ember — the palette is a tonal ladder of one hue; label the series or vary the line dash.
**Don't** communicate status or error by color alone — pair it with a message or icon.
**Don't** style Penpot text with a typography asset or an off-scale face — bind a `typography.*` token.
**Don't** maintain or introduce a light theme unless the product requirements explicitly change.
